speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when the swelling and pain in your right ring finger started and if there was any specific injury or event that triggered it?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did you hear or feel a "pop" at the time of injury, and are you currently unable to fully straighten or bend the finger? I need to assess if there is tendon damage or a fracture.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text: You are describing classic signs of a mallet finger, where the extensor tendon is avulsed from the bone. I will order an X-ray to check for any associated fracture of the distal phalanx. REQUEST TEST: X-Ray_Ring_Finger

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical history. Social history: Student and active in sports, particularly football. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, numbness, or tingling in the affected finger. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: The X-ray confirms no fracture, and your symptoms of an extended resting position with inability to flex the DIP joint are classic for a soft tissue injury. DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
